ideas.title: Terraforming Mars Orbital Production Dial Tower
ideas.concept: A stackable set of 6 rotating click-stop rings (one per resource: MegaCredits, Steel, Titanium, Plants, Power, Heat), each showing its current production level through a small window, replacing the cardboard player-board production track with a tactile turning tower.
ideas.rationale: Terraforming Mars has held a top-10 BGG rank for years running and is one of the most-owned heavy euros on the site, so its owner base is large and demonstrably still active (frequent new expansions: Ares Expedition, Big Box reprints). Web search for 'Terraforming Mars rotating resource production dial 3d print' returned only static cube holders and resource bins (Thingiverse thing:2338058, MakerWorld Terraforming Mars tiles set) -- no rotating-dial mechanism for this game, so this fills a specific gap rather than a category nobody has touched.
ideas.differentiation: Existing free designs for this game are all static cube trays or bins that still require manually counting/moving cubes each generation. This replaces that with a single rotating dial per resource with tactile click-stops, a mechanism not present in the results checked (Thingiverse, MakerWorld, Printables, Cults3D, MyMiniFactory searches). Claim is scoped to 'no dial-based production tracker found for this title,' not an absolute market-wide claim.
ideas.producibility_notes: 8 total parts: 6 identical dial rings + 1 base + 1 cap, snap-stacked on a central spline. Each ring has its own printed-in-place flex-tab click detent (repeated joint, N=6) -- justified because the detent engages a large-diameter (30mm) ring against light finger torque, low load per click, a common and reliable pattern in existing click-counter prints. Single color body with debossed numerals (no multi-color needed); critical tolerance is the ring-to-spline snap fit (0.15-0.2mm clearance).
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~4.0 hr, ~120g PLA (~$3.60 filament at $0.03/g) plus labor. Sell at $24/unit (1 per player) or $85 for a 4-pack. A buyer of a $70+ heavy euro who already owns sleeves and organizer inserts for it is a proven high-spend accessory buyer, so a $24 tactile upgrade against ~$4 of material is a plausible margin.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a stackable tabletop resource-production tracker consisting of 6 identical rotating dial rings (each ~30mm outer diameter, 18mm tall) threaded onto a central fixed spline between a base cap and a top cap, for a total assembled height of about 130mm and diameter of 40mm. Each ring rotates independently and displays a single number (0-10) through a small cutout window on the adjacent fixed sleeve, advancing one increment per click via a printed-in-place flex-tab detent molded into the ring's inner bore. Purpose: a per-player accessory for the board game Terraforming Mars, replacing the cardboard production track with a tactile turning dial for each of the 6 resource types (MegaCredits, Steel, Titanium, Plants, Power, Heat); used by adult hobby board gamers during play. Style: minimal/utilitarian sci-fi, clean cylindrical geometry with debossed (recessed, not embossed) numerals for high contrast without needing paint; single flat color per unit, no ornamentation. Technical specification: overall assembly approx 40mm diameter x 130mm tall, 8 total printed parts (6 identical rotation rings + 1 base + 1 cap), single material/single color FDM PLA, no hardware or inserts. Critical features the modeler must get right: the ring-to-spline snap-fit clearance must be 0.15-0.2mm for smooth rotation without wobble; each ring's flex-tab detent must be at least 0.8mm thick at its base to survive repeated clicking without fatigue failure; the viewing window cutout must align precisely with the printed numerals at each of the 11 click positions (0 through 10); assembly order is base cap first, then rings stacked bottom to top, then top cap snapped on last, all rings must rotate freely after final assembly with no support material trapped in the detent cavities.

ideas.title: Catan Probability Setup Rack & Claim Tracker
ideas.concept: A flat tray with 18 hex-shaped wells for the number tokens, arranged into 3 concentric color-molded probability rings (high/mid/low pip count) to speed up balanced board setup, with two small rotating pointer dials mounted at the center to track which player currently holds Longest Road and Largest Army.
ideas.rationale: Catan is the best-selling hobby board game franchise in history (Kosmos/Catan Studio cite over 32 million copies sold worldwide across editions), giving it the largest plausible owner base of any title in this batch. Search for 'Catan harbor tile rack flip lock 3d print' turned up only static frame borders and interlocking tile sets (Thingiverse thing:2315602, thing:2525047); no result combined a probability-sorted setup tray with a Longest-Road/Largest-Army claim tracker.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Catan prints are either full board frames/interlocking tile systems or standalone victory-point trackers (an Etsy 'Catan Victory Points Tracker' exists for VP counting, not for the two contested-title cards). Pairing probability-tier setup guidance with a physical claim-tracker for the two most-forgotten rules elements in Catan (who currently has Longest Road/Largest Army) was not found in the sources checked; claim is scoped to that specific combination, not a blanket 'nothing exists for Catan' statement.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 parts: 1 flat tray + 2 identical small pointer discs, each disc friction-fits onto a printed boss at the tray center (N=2 repeated pivot joints, low risk since discs are lightweight and pivot diameter is generous at 5mm). Single color print with debossed pip-count rings and player-color paint dots optional; no hardware needed.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~3.5 hr, ~90g PLA (~$2.70 filament). Sell at $19/unit. Catan owners already buy third-party organizer trays and expansion accessories at retail (established behavior on Etsy/Amazon for this title), so $19 for a setup-speed + rules-tracking tool against ~$3 material cost is consistent with what that market already pays for Catan-specific inserts.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a flat setup tray, roughly 220mm across and 10mm thick, with 18 hexagonal recessed wells sized to hold standard Settlers of Catan number tokens (approx 24mm diameter, 3mm thick each), arranged in 3 concentric rings distinguished by a debossed border pattern: an inner ring of 4 wells for the highest-probability numbers (6 and 8), a middle ring of 8 wells for mid-probability numbers (4,5,9,10), and an outer ring of 6 wells for low-probability numbers (2,3,11,12). At the tray's center, mount two small (28mm diameter) rotating pointer discs side by side on separate 5mm friction-fit posts, each disc printed with a single arrow and free-spinning by hand, used to indicate which player currently holds the Longest Road and Largest Army cards respectively. Purpose: an accessory for the board game Catan (Settlers of Catan) used by the group during game setup to balance number-token placement by probability tier, and during play as a shared reminder of who holds the two contested achievement cards; for board game hobbyists and family game-night hosts. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color body, debossed geometric ring dividers and numerals, no ornamentation beyond functional markings. Technical specification: overall tray approx 220mm x 220mm x 10mm, 3 total printed parts (1 tray + 2 identical pointer discs), single material/single color FDM PLA, no hardware or metal inserts required. Critical features: each pointer disc's center post must have a 0.15mm printing clearance for smooth hand-rotation without being loose enough to spin freely on its own; the hex wells must be sized with 0.3mm clearance over standard Catan token dimensions so tokens seat and lift out without sticking; assembly is simply press-fitting the two discs onto their posts after printing, no glue required.

ideas.title: Splendor Reserve Privacy Shield & Noble Display Stand
ideas.concept: A folded two-sided stand: the front-facing side toward its owner is an open shelf holding up to 3 reserved cards visible only to that player, while an opaque back panel blocks other players' view of those same cards; the reverse side of the stand displays the game's 5 noble tiles upright for shared visibility.
ideas.rationale: Splendor was a 2014 Spiel des Jahres nominee and remains one of the most-owned gateway games on BGG with a large casual-to-hobbyist crossover audience, meaning broad familiarity and a big pool of existing owners. Search for 'Splendor reserved card privacy shield stand 3d print' returned only general card/chip holders and travel organizers (Cults3D 'Splendor Game card and chip holders', printables Splendor Travel Case); no privacy-shield mechanism for reserved cards appeared in results.
ideas.differentiation: All existing Splendor prints found are storage/organizer or generic upright card-holder designs; none block opposing players' view of reserved cards, which is a real information-hiding gap in the base game (reserved cards are normally kept face-down or awkwardly hidden by hand). Combining that privacy function with the noble-tile display on the reverse was not found in any listing checked; claim is scoped accordingly.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1-2 parts: a single print-in-place hinged panel (front shelf folds relative to the back-facing screen) or a 2-part slot-together stand if the hinge proves unreliable at scale -- default to the simpler single-hinge version since only one joint is needed. Single color, no hardware.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~2.5 hr, ~70g PLA (~$2.10 filament). Sell at $16/unit, or $55 for a 4-pack covering a full table. Splendor's broad, casual-leaning owner base (including many non-hobbyist gift buyers) already pays $10-20 for simple gem-token organizers on Etsy, so a $16 gameplay-improving accessory against ~$2 material is a reasonable price the same buyer segment already demonstrates willingness to pay.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a single free-standing card/tile stand, approximately 180mm wide x 110mm tall x 55mm deep, built around one print-in-place living hinge down the center. One face of the stand has a shallow forward-tilted shelf (70mm wide slot, 5mm deep) that holds up to 3 sleeved or unsleeved standard playing cards upright and angled toward the owning player only; directly behind that shelf, an opaque solid panel blocks the view of those same cards from the opposite side of the table. The reverse face of the stand (the side facing away from the card shelf) has 5 shallow slots arranged in a row, each sized to hold one square tile (approx 45mm x 45mm x 8mm) upright and visible to all players. Purpose: a two-function accessory for the board game Splendor, used by an individual player to privately hold their reserved development cards during play while simultaneously displaying the shared noble tiles for the whole table to see; for board game hobbyists and casual/family players. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color, smooth rounded edges, no ornamentation. Technical specification: overall dimensions approx 180mm x 110mm x 55mm, 1 printed part using a single living hinge (print-in-place, no assembly), single material/single color FDM PLA. Critical features: the living hinge must be 0.6-0.8mm thick at the flex point to survive repeated folding without cracking; the card shelf slot must have 1mm clearance over standard sleeved card thickness; the tile slots must have 0.3mm clearance over the noble tile dimensions so tiles seat firmly but are easy to remove by hand; the part must print flat with the hinge oriented along the grain of the print bed to avoid layer-adhesion failure at the hinge line.

ideas.title: Chess In-Play Captured Piece Value Tray
ideas.concept: A slim two-lane tray (one lane per color) that sits along the edge of a chessboard during a game, each lane subdivided into 4 labeled bays by piece value (pawns, minor pieces, rooks, queen) so captured pieces are sorted as they come off the board instead of piled loosely, letting either player read material balance at a glance.
ideas.rationale: Chess has had a well-documented resurgence in mainstream attention since the 2020 Netflix series The Queen's Gambit, with Chess.com and Lichess both publicly reporting multi-year user growth continuing into the mid-2020s, keeping the buyer pool of casual and club chess players unusually large for a centuries-old game. Search for 'chess captured pieces organizer tray in-play sorted 3d print' returned only complete chess-set designs and post-game storage boxes (MakerWorld 'Minimalist Chess Set', various storage-focused sets); no in-play, value-sorted capture tray appeared.
ideas.differentiation: Chess accessory prints found in search are overwhelmingly full playable sets or post-game piece-storage boxes; the closest reference was a single forum mention that 'a lid could use magnets to hold captured pieces' as an incidental afterthought, not a dedicated value-sorted in-play tray. This product's specific angle -- an active-play tool distinct from storage -- was not found as an existing product.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 identical tray halves (one per color), no moving parts, no hardware, single color print. This is a low-risk producibility profile: flat geometry, no joints, no features under 1mm, straightforward to slice and print reliably.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~2.0 hr, ~60g PLA (~$1.80 filament). Sell at $14/unit (pair). Chess sets themselves range from $15 gift-shop sets to $200+ hobbyist sets, and buyers of mid-tier sets ($30-80) regularly add small accessories; $14 for a functional in-play organizer against ~$1.80 material cost fits that established accessory price band.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a pair of identical slim rectangular trays, each approximately 300mm long x 60mm wide x 15mm tall, meant to sit end-to-end or side-by-side along the outer edge of a standard chessboard. Each tray is divided by raised internal walls into 4 unequal bays sized to nest standard chess pieces sorted by captured value: a wide bay for up to 8 pawns, a bay for up to 2 knights and 2 bishops, a bay for up to 2 rooks, and a small bay for 1 queen. Purpose: an in-play accessory for the board game chess, used by either player during a live game to organize captured opponent pieces by value as they are taken, so material balance can be read at a glance without recounting; for casual and club chess players. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color, smooth chamfered bay openings for easy piece placement and removal, no ornamentation. Technical specification: two total printed parts, each approx 300mm x 60mm x 15mm (one tray per color side), single material/single color FDM PLA, no hardware or assembly required -- each tray prints and ships as one solid piece. Critical features: bay wall thickness must be at least 2mm for print strength; each bay floor must be recessed at least 8mm deep to keep captured pieces from sliding out when the tray is bumped; bay openings must be sized with at least 3mm clearance over standard Staunton piece base diameters (pawn approx 25mm, queen approx 35mm) to accommodate common tournament-size sets without requiring exact piece-set matching.

ideas.title: Ticket to Ride Destination Completion Flip Clip
ideas.concept: A small clip that attaches to the top edge of a player's Destination Ticket card and holds a single flip-tab printed red on one face and green on the other; the player flips the tab from red to green the moment that route is completed, giving an at-a-glance status indicator without re-reading the card each turn.
ideas.rationale: Ticket to Ride won the 2004 Spiel des Jahres and remains one of the most widely-owned gateway board games in North America and Europe, with Days of Wonder continuing to release new map expansions into the 2020s, indicating a large and still-active owner base. Search for 'Ticket to Ride destination ticket completion slide tracker 3d print' returned only card holders, box inserts, and a sliding train-piece storage box (MyMiniFactory 'Ticket To Ride Sliding Box for Trains'); no per-card completion-status indicator was found.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Ticket to Ride prints organize train pieces or hold cards upright for visibility; none track completion status of individual destination tickets. This product's flip-tab status indicator, attached directly to the card rather than a separate tracking sheet, was not found among the designs checked.
ideas.producibility_notes: Sold as a set of 12 identical single-part clips (covers a full hand of tickets across base game and an expansion). Each clip is one printed part using a single printed-in-place flex snap to hold its flip-tab in either of two bistable positions -- this is the low-risk 'single flex/snap joint, repeated across many identical small parts' producibility pattern rather than a pin-and-pivot mechanism. Two-color print recommended (red/green tab) but a single-color version with a painted or debossed indicator is also viable.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~3.0 hr for a set of 12, ~50g PLA total (~$1.50 filament). Sell at $15 per 12-pack. Ticket to Ride players commonly buy card sleeves and small accessories in multi-packs at similar price points on Etsy, so $15 for a functional gameplay aid against $1.50 material is consistent with that market's existing accessory spend.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a small single-piece clip, approximately 40mm wide x 20mm tall x 8mm deep, that slides over and grips the top edge of a standard Ticket to Ride Destination Ticket card (card thickness approx 0.3mm, standard playing-card width). Built into the clip is a small flip-tab (approx 15mm x 10mm) connected by a printed-in-place flex hinge that snaps into one of two stable positions: tab-down showing a red face, or tab-up showing a green face, changed by the player pressing the tab from one side. Purpose: a per-card status indicator for the board game Ticket to Ride, used by a player during the game to mark whether a specific destination ticket route has been completed, sold as a set for use across a full hand of tickets; for board game hobbyists and family game-night players. Style: minimal/utilitarian, bold red/green color contrast on the flip-tab for at-a-glance readability, no ornamentation. Technical specification: sold as a set of 12 identical printed parts, each approx 40mm x 20mm x 8mm, ideally printed in two colors (red and green tab faces) via a color-change print or dual-extrusion; a single-color fallback version uses debossed '+' and 'X' symbols on each tab face instead of color. No hardware or assembly required per unit. Critical features: the card-edge gripping slot must have 0.4-0.5mm clearance over standard card stock thickness so the clip holds firmly without tearing the card on insertion; the flex hinge connecting the flip-tab must be 0.6mm thick to survive at least 50 flips per game across many games without fatigue cracking; the two bistable detent bumps must be shaped so the tab requires a deliberate press to move, preventing accidental flips during normal card handling.

ideas.title: Pandemic Outbreak Dial Cube Tray
ideas.concept: A disease-cube storage tray with 4 color-coded wells (matching Pandemic's blue, yellow, black, and red disease colors) topped by a rotating lid dial that mirrors the game's outbreak track from 0 to 8, letting players advance outbreaks directly on the box insert instead of the board's small printed track.
ideas.rationale: Pandemic is one of the best-selling modern cooperative board games, with publisher Z-Man Games having sold well over 8 million units across editions according to widely reported industry figures, and remains a top-100 BGG title with active expansions (On the Brink, In the Lab, Fall of Rome) continuing to be produced. Search for 'Pandemic outbreak counter rotating dial lid 3d print' returned disease-cube organizers with simple lids and separate generic dial counters, but no design combining the two into one lid-mounted outbreak dial for this specific game.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Pandemic prints are cube-storage organizers (with or without magnetic lids) or are unrelated to outbreak tracking; generic rotating dial counters exist for other purposes but were not found built into a Pandemic disease-cube tray lid specifically. Claim is scoped to that specific combination not appearing in the sources checked.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts: 1 tray body with 4 wells + 1 rotating lid with a single printed-in-place click detent tracking positions 0-8 (one joint, low risk given generous 60mm lid diameter and light detent load). Single color body, debossed track numerals; no hardware.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~3.0 hr, ~85g PLA (~$2.55 filament). Sell at $18/unit. Pandemic owners already buy third-party cube organizers on Etsy/Printables-adjacent storefronts at $15-25, so this combined tray+tracker at $18 against ~$2.55 material fits the demonstrated price band for this exact accessory category on this exact game.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a rectangular storage tray, approximately 130mm x 130mm x 30mm, divided into 4 equal square wells each sized to hold approximately 24 wooden disease cubes (8mm cubes) in one color group (blue, yellow, black, red). A round lid, 60mm in diameter, sits centered on top of the tray and rotates independently, with a printed arrow pointer on the lid aligned against 9 numbered positions (0 through 8) printed around the lid's mounting collar on the tray, replicating the game's outbreak track. Purpose: a combined storage and gameplay-tracking accessory for the cooperative board game Pandemic, used by the player group during a session to both store disease cubes compactly in the box and track the current outbreak count directly on the tray lid instead of the board's small printed track; for cooperative board game hobbyists. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color body with debossed track numerals and a contrasting-color arrow pointer (2-color print recommended, single-color debossed fallback acceptable), no ornamentation. Technical specification: 2 total printed parts (1 four-well tray + 1 rotating lid dial), overall footprint approx 130mm x 130mm x 30mm assembled, single material FDM PLA. Critical features: the lid's center rotation boss must have 0.15-0.2mm clearance for smooth manual rotation without wobble; the click detent must be a printed-in-place flex tab at least 0.8mm thick engaging 9 shallow notches spaced evenly around the collar; well wall thickness must be at least 2mm; assembly is a simple press-fit of the lid onto the tray's center post after printing, no glue or hardware required.

ideas.title: Root Faction Reputation & Dominance Stand
ideas.concept: A per-faction stand combining a rotating victory-point ring (spun against a fixed pointer to track progress toward the 30-point win condition, off the shared and often crowded cardboard score track) with a slotted base that displays that faction's unplayed Dominance card upright once it becomes eligible to play.
ideas.rationale: Root, designed by Cole Wehrle and published by Leder Games, has held a consistently strong BGG ranking (typically within the site's top 50 strategy games) since its 2018 release and has sustained multiple retail expansions (Riverfolk, Underworld, Marauder, Clockwork) through the mid-2020s, indicating an active, dedicated fanbase willing to invest in the game long-term. Search for 'Root board game dominance card flip stand reputation slider 3d print' found VP marker stands and general card holders (Printables 'Root - Board Game Organizer'), but no design combining a rotating per-faction score ring with a dominance-card display slot.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Root prints are either full organizers/inserts for game pieces or simple upright card holders; the specific combination of an individual rotating score-progress ring per faction plus a Dominance-card display slot was not found among the results checked. This targets a documented real pain point (the shared cardboard score track becomes crowded and hard to read with 3-6 factions on it), narrowed to a specific mechanism, not a claim that no Root accessories exist at all.
ideas.producibility_notes: Sold as a 4-pack (typical player count); each unit is 2 parts (base with card slot + rotating outer ring, single friction-fit joint per unit, N=4 total repeated joints across the pack -- low risk given generous 50mm ring diameter and light load). Single color per unit, debossed 0-30 point track.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~5.0 hr for a 4-pack, ~140g PLA (~$4.20 filament). Sell at $28 for the 4-pack. Root's dedicated fanbase already supports a secondary market of official and third-party upgrade components (custom meeples, faction boards) sold at $20-40 per set on Etsy, so this accessory's price is consistent with what that specific buyer base already spends on faction-specific upgrades.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a set of 4 identical two-part stands. Each stand has a base, approximately 60mm x 50mm x 15mm, with a vertical slot (3mm wide, 45mm tall) to hold one standard-size card upright and visible to the table, plus a raised circular collar (50mm diameter) around which a separate rotating ring sits. The ring, also 50mm in diameter with a printed arrow, rotates against 31 numbered positions (0 through 30) printed on the base collar beneath it, tracking a single faction's cumulative score toward the 30-point win condition. Purpose: a per-faction accessory for the asymmetric strategy board game Root, used by each player during the game to track their own victory-point progress on an individual dial (rather than a single crowded shared track) and to display their unplayed Dominance card upright once eligible; for hobbyist strategy board gamers. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color per unit body with debossed track numerals, no ornamentation beyond functional markings. Technical specification: 4 total identical assemblies (8 printed parts: 4 bases + 4 rotating rings), each assembled unit approx 60mm x 60mm x 20mm, single material FDM PLA, one color per unit (may vary color across the 4 units to match faction colors). Critical features: the ring-to-base collar clearance must be 0.15-0.2mm for smooth rotation without excessive play; the card slot must have 0.4mm clearance over standard card thickness; base wall thickness minimum 2mm; assembly is press-fitting each ring onto its base collar after printing, no adhesive or hardware needed.

ideas.title: Monopoly Banker Station: Cash Tray & Deed Carousel
ideas.concept: A two-tier banker's station: the bottom tier is a cash tray with denomination-sized bill wells plus a bin for houses and hotels, and the top tier is a rotating carousel disc with 22 upright slots that displays every property deed card sorted by color group, spun by the banker to locate any deed instantly during trades.
ideas.rationale: Monopoly is documented by Guinness World Records and publisher Hasbro as the best-selling commercially produced board game in the world, with well over 275 million copies sold since 1935, giving it an enormous and constantly refreshed buyer pool through gift-giving occasions (holidays, housewarming, family game night). Search for 'Monopoly banker cash tray rotating property deed carousel 3d print' returned multiple banker money/property trays but explicitly no rotating deed-carousel design among the results checked.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Monopoly banker trays organize cash and sometimes flat property cards in static slots; a rotating carousel that lets the banker spin to any color group's deed cards during active trading was not found in the designs checked, and search explicitly noted the absence of a rotating variant.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 main parts (tray base + rotating carousel disc on a center post, single friction-fit joint, no bearing needed given the light load) plus a set of identical divider inserts for the cash wells (many small identical parts, low risk). Single color print.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~5.0 hr, ~150g PLA (~$4.50 filament). Sell at $26/unit. Monopoly's mass-market gift-buyer base already regularly purchases $15-30 third-party organizer/banker-tray accessories on Etsy for this exact game, so $26 against ~$4.50 material is consistent with an established price point for this accessory category on the world's best-selling board game.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a two-tier banker's station for Monopoly. The bottom tier is a rectangular tray, approximately 250mm x 180mm x 40mm, divided into 6 denomination wells (for $1, $5, $10, $20, $50, $100 bills) each with a removable divider insert, plus one additional bin sized for houses and hotels. Mounted on a center post rising from one end of the tray is a rotating carousel disc, 150mm in diameter and 60mm tall, with 22 upright slots arranged around its circumference and grouped into the 8 standard Monopoly color groups (with small color-matched dividers between groups), sized to hold the game's property deed cards standing on edge. Purpose: a banking accessory for the board game Monopoly, used by whichever player serves as banker to organize cash by denomination and to quickly locate any property deed card during trades by spinning the carousel; for family and casual board game players, especially useful for game nights and gift purchases. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color, clean rectilinear tray with a cylindrical carousel, no ornamentation beyond functional dividers. Technical specification: overall footprint approx 250mm x 180mm x 100mm assembled (tray plus mounted carousel), total printed parts: 2 main bodies (tray + carousel disc) plus 6 identical cash-well dividers = 8 parts, single material/single color FDM PLA, no metal hardware. Critical features: the carousel's center post must have 0.15-0.2mm clearance in the disc's mounting bore for smooth hand-spun rotation without wobble under the light weight of paper deed cards; deed card slots must be at least 1mm wider than standard deed card thickness with sleeve compatibility; cash well width must match current-edition Monopoly bill dimensions with 2mm side clearance; assembly is press-fitting the carousel onto the tray's post and the 6 dividers into the cash wells, no glue required.

ideas.title: Kingdom Card Mechanical Randomizer Wheel
ideas.concept: A hand-crank drum randomizer holding a full deckbuilding game's card-type token set behind a small viewing window; spinning the drum and stopping it at a click-detent reveals one selection at a time, used to draw a random set of 10 Kingdom cards for game setup without shuffling loose cards or using a phone app.
ideas.rationale: Dominion, which originated and still anchors the deckbuilding genre, won the 2009 Spiel des Jahres and remains in active publication with new expansions (Rising Sun released 2023) still being released by Rio Grande Games/publisher, indicating the genre and this title specifically retain an ongoing, currently-buying fanbase. Search for 'Dominion kingdom card randomizer wheel mechanical selector 3d print' returned exclusively digital tools -- phone apps and websites (Google Play listings, GitHub randomizer repos) -- with no physical 3D-printed mechanical randomizer found among the results checked.
ideas.differentiation: Every existing Dominion randomizer found in search is software (an app or website); this is a tactile physical alternative for players who want a tabletop-native setup ritual instead of pulling out a phone mid-game-night, a gap the search results support (no physical print-based competitor surfaced) though this is stated as an absence-of-evidence finding, not a guarantee no such product exists anywhere.
ideas.producibility_notes: 4 parts: drum body + crank handle + viewing-window slide gate + printed-in-place pawl/click mechanism (single joint type, one instance, low risk). Single color print; the card-type tokens themselves are not included (labeled with a dry-erase or sticker system by the buyer, or offered as a separate blank-token add-on) to avoid needing hundreds of card-specific inserts.
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~5.0 hr, ~140g PLA (~$4.20 filament). Sell at $27/unit. Dominion players already buy card-organizer boxes and expansion-sorting inserts at $20-35 on Etsy for this title, so a novel physical setup tool at $27 against ~$4.20 material sits within that established willingness-to-pay band for Dominion-specific accessories.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a hand-crank drum randomizer, approximately 150mm wide x 100mm tall x 100mm deep, consisting of a rotating internal drum that holds up to 40 small labeled tokens (each token slot approx 20mm x 30mm) around its circumference, enclosed in an outer housing with a single viewing window (25mm x 35mm) on top through which one token is visible at a time. A side-mounted crank handle rotates the drum, which advances via a printed-in-place spring pawl engaging notches at each token position, giving a tactile click at every stop. A small sliding gate covers the window when not in use. Purpose: a physical setup tool for deckbuilding card games such as Dominion, used by a group of players before a session to randomly select a subset of cards (e.g. 10 Kingdom cards) from the game's full card pool without using a phone app or shuffling loose cards; for hobbyist board/card gamers, especially deckbuilding-genre players. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color housing, simple geometric crank handle, no thematic ornamentation so it works across multiple deckbuilding titles. Technical specification: overall assembled size approx 150mm x 100mm x 100mm, 4 total printed parts (drum + outer housing + crank handle + slide gate), single material/single color FDM PLA, no metal hardware -- the crank handle attaches via a printed D-shaft press-fit into the drum's axle. Critical features: the drum axle-to-housing bearing surface needs 0.2mm clearance for smooth hand-cranked rotation; the spring pawl must be at least 1mm thick at its base to survive repeated use without breaking, and must engage cleanly with 40 evenly spaced notches around the drum's inner rim; the viewing window and slide gate must have a 0.3mm sliding clearance so the gate moves freely without falling out; assembly order is drum first, then housing halves around it, then crank handle press-fit onto the exposed axle end last.

ideas.title: Playmat Wind-Lock Corner Clip Set
ideas.concept: A set of 4 low-profile clips that snap over the corners of a standard trading-card-game playmat (approx 355mm x 610mm fabric or neoprene mat) and grip lightly onto the table edge or add a weighted base, preventing the mat from sliding, curling, or lifting in wind during outdoor or convention play.
ideas.rationale: Magic: The Gathering is documented by Hasbro/Wizards of the Coast as the best-selling trading card game franchise with a large, active competitive and casual tournament scene (regular conventions, store-organized play, and outdoor meetup culture are well-documented parts of TCG hobbyist life), and playmats are a mature, high-volume accessory category on their own (Inked Gaming and similar vendors sell them as a standalone product line), indicating a large buyer pool already spending on playmat-adjacent accessories. Search for 'playmat corner weight clip wind outdoor con card game 3d print' explicitly returned a result noting 'custom corner weight clip designs specifically for wind protection may still be a niche product opportunity,' and no dedicated wind/edge-lock clip product was found among storage-focused playmat holders.
ideas.differentiation: The playmat accessories found in search are exclusively storage tubes/cases for transporting rolled mats; none address the in-use problem of mats sliding or lifting during outdoor or convention play. This targets that specific unaddressed use case rather than the well-covered storage category.
ideas.producibility_notes: Set of 4 identical single-part clips, each a simple snap-over-edge C-clip geometry, no moving parts, no hardware, single color print -- a low-risk producibility profile (many identical small parts, one flagged tolerance, no joints).
ideas.margin_case: Print time ~1.5 hr for a set of 4, ~40g PLA (~$1.20 filament). Sell at $12/set. TCG players already buy $30-60 playmats as a standalone accessory category and separately buy $10-15 mat tubes/cases for transport, so a $12 in-use accessory against $1.20 material fits the same buyer's demonstrated per-accessory spend for this hobby.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a set of 4 identical low-profile corner clips, each approximately 45mm x 45mm x 20mm, shaped as a C-clip that slides over the corner of a fabric or neoprene playmat (mat thickness approx 2-3mm) and grips both the top and bottom faces of the mat corner with a spring-loaded lip, while a small flat foot extends outward from the clip to either rest under a table edge for friction or to add ballast weight (the foot cavity is designed to optionally hold a printed-in weight insert or a small embedded coin/washer, left as an open cavity in the base design). Purpose: an accessory for trading card game playmats (Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon, Yu-Gi-Oh and similar standard-size mats, approx 355mm x 610mm), used by players during outdoor or convention play to keep the mat from sliding, curling, or lifting in wind or from table bumps; for competitive and casual TCG hobbyists. Style: minimal/utilitarian, single flat color, low-profile rounded geometry that does not obstruct play area, no ornamentation. Technical specification: set of 4 identical printed parts, each approx 45mm x 45mm x 20mm, single material/single color FDM PLA, no assembly or hardware required (each clip is one solid piece, printed with a flexible-enough wall to snap over the mat edge by hand). Critical features: the C-clip's mat-gripping lip opening must have 0.3-0.5mm negative clearance relative to typical playmat thickness (2-3mm) so the clip grips firmly via light spring tension without needing separate hardware; wall thickness at the flex point of the C-clip must be 1.2-1.5mm to allow repeated opening without snapping when printed in standard PLA; the outward foot must be flat-bottomed and at least 15mm x 15mm in contact area for table-edge friction stability.
